argument.statement: Syrian political life stayed dominated by a particular urban elite despite Ottoman’s end and French control, shaped by conflicts between France and Syrian nationalists and between liberal and radical nationalism.

book.rationale: The book primarily discusses the historical context of Syria under French Mandate, focusing on national politics and conflicts, which aligns it most closely with History while also incorporating elements of World History and Politics & Government.
book.summary: Why did Syrian political life continue to be dominated by a particular urban elite even after the dramatic changes following the end of four hundred years of Ottoman rule and the imposition of French control? Philip Khoury's comprehensive work discusses this and other questions in the framework of two related conflicts--one between France and the Syrian nationalists, and the other between liberal and radical nationalism. Originally published in 1987.
